objective: T-20260929-51 step 1: test whether short IWM/RSP/IJR/XRT/KRE hedged with trailing-beta long SPY has a tradable Sharpe in 2024-2026 after 10 bp per side and a 0.5%/yr ETF borrow fee, or whether the Kargarzadeh et al. 2026 small-cap drift is a benchmark artifact. No return is computed in this dossier.

sources.core_claim: Neutral-news covered stocks trail their beta benchmark by -0.92%/month among small caps (-0.58% mid, -0.34% large); quiet stock-days drift -0.74/-0.88/-0.59%. Table 6 'short any covered small cap', beta-hedged to SPY, 2023-2026: Sharpe 1.35 gross, 0.78 at 20 bp per side. Cost model is a flat fee per side; borrow fees and locates not modelled.
sources.credibility: arXiv preprint, not peer reviewed; PDF read locally in full sections 5.2/5.6/Table 6
sources.project_applicability: Origin of the direction. Step 1 of this iteration tests the ETF-level version of the same benchmark drift with an explicit borrow fee.
sources.reflection: Single sample 2023-2026, single-beta SPY benchmark; the authors themselves call the drift the residual of the benchmark. Decays if mega-cap leadership reverses; no borrow fee, so the 0.78 is an upper bound.

sources.core_claim: Size premium is weak, time-varying and weakened after the early 1980s, concentrated in microcaps; it becomes stable once quality/junk is controlled.
sources.credibility: AQR working paper (published JFE 2018); abstract and introduction read locally
sources.project_applicability: Prior that an unconditional short-small-cap spread is a regime bet on size, not a stable premium; the unhedged-for-quality IWM/SPY spread is expected to be weak outside regimes.
sources.reflection: Long-only-factor framing, not a short-basket after-borrow test; documents decay of the raw size effect.

sources.core_claim: Cheap-minus-expensive-to-short portfolio earns 1.43%/month gross, 0.91% net of fees; anomalies effectively disappear within the 80% of stocks with low short fees and are amplified among high-fee stocks.
sources.credibility: NBER working paper, abstract read locally
sources.project_applicability: Short-side returns of stocks concentrate where borrow is expensive: the easy-to-borrow (ETB) subset that Alpaca permits should show a much smaller drift than an all-stock basket. Motivates the ETB proxy tiers in step 2 and the 5/15% borrow grid.
sources.reflection: US 2000s-2010s sample; borrow-fee data vendor-specific; effect is compensation for short risk, may not carry to 2023-26.

sources.core_claim: Stocks with high borrow fees tend to decline, but high borrow fees largely offset the profits from shorting them: the short strategy is profitable gross, roughly flat net of borrow fees.
sources.credibility: practitioner blog with IB borrow-fee archive 2018-04..2024-04; Alphalens methodology
sources.project_applicability: Borrow fee must be deducted per candidate; only ETB tiers belong in the tradable test.
sources.reflection: Interactive Brokers rates, US ex-microcap, 2018-2024; not Alpaca's fee schedule.

sources.core_claim: Smaller, volatile, illiquid stocks are much more expensive to borrow; fees for a single name change sharply through time (GameStop 1% in Jan 2019, much higher by Jan 2021).
sources.project_applicability: Borrow-fee grid {0,5%,15%} and the short-squeeze month check (2021-01/02) in step 2.
sources.reflection: Own borrow-cost classifier, no net-of-fee return number.

sources.core_claim: Shorting small caps after a -10% earnings day (8,861 trades, 2,615 stocks, 2011-2026) lost money after costs: mean -1.48% per trade, 48.3% hit rate; all 31 preregistered variants stayed negative.
sources.credibility: independent backtest write-up, 8,861 small-cap short trades 2011-2026
sources.project_applicability: Independent negative evidence on stock-level small-cap shorts in exactly the paper's window; this unconditional baseline is the placebo for such tests.
sources.reflection: Event-conditioned, not an unconditional basket; unhedged trades.

sources.core_claim: Shorting needs a margin account with >= $2,000; Alpaca distinguishes easy-to-borrow (ETB) and hard-to-borrow (HTB) securities, charges a daily stock borrow fee and provides a locate workflow for HTB names.
sources.project_applicability: Execution constraint: only ETB names are shortable without a locate; index ETFs are ETB. Short proceeds earn no interest.
sources.reflection: Fee schedule is current, not historical; the 0.5%/yr ETF assumption is preregistered, not read from a fee table.

sources.core_claim: Stock loan market 2000-2001: most stocks are cheap to borrow (loan fees near 0.25%) and a small share are 'special' with high fees and recalls.
sources.credibility: Journal of Financial Economics 66(2-3); found via WebSearch (SSRN page returned 403 to a direct fetch, so the abstract is a search summary, not an opened snapshot)
sources.project_applicability: Supports a low borrow fee for liquid ETF/large stocks and a stress grid for small ones.
sources.reflection: 2000-2001 sample only; the 0.25% figure is from the paper's well-known result, not re-read here (marked search_snippet_only).
